body: Draws the heights `Z` over a grid as a surface of four-sided faces, coloured by height through the colormap. The grid is given by `X` and `Y` (matrices from `meshgrid`, or vectors along the columns and rows), or is the row and column numbers when only `Z` is given. Drag in the figure to turn the view; `shading interp` smooths the colours and hides the edges, and `view` sets the angle.
syntax: Heights over the row and column numbers.
Coloured by `C` instead of by height.
With surface properties, such as `'EdgeColor'`, `'FaceAlpha'` and `'FaceColor'`.
inputs: The grid: matrices the size of `Z`, or vectors whose lengths match its columns and rows.

examples.title: A function over a grid
Smooth shading and a colour scale
See-through faces, seen from above at an angle

body: Like `surf`, but draws only the edges of the faces, coloured by height, so that the parts behind show through the net.
syntax: Heights over the row and column numbers.

examples.title: A saddle as a net
examples.code:
[X, Y] = meshgrid(-1:0.1:1);
mesh(X, Y, X.^2 - Y.^2)

examples.title: A ripple

body: Draws lines along which `Z` has the same value, as a map shows heights: close lines mean steep slopes. Without levels, the levels are chosen from the data; `n` asks for about that many, and a vector gives the levels themselves. `clabel` writes the levels on the lines.
syntax: Over the row and column numbers.
The given levels (`[v v]` for the one level `v`).
With the contour matrix `C` (for `clabel`) and the contour object.

examples.title: Levels of a function, labelled

body: Like `contour`, with the spaces between the levels filled in the colours of the colormap.
syntax: Over the row and column numbers.
Over the grid, with about `n` levels.

examples.title: A filled map with a colour scale

pages.summary: Show a matrix as an image, its values scaled to the colormap.
body: Each element is a coloured cell: the smallest value takes the first colour of the colormap and the largest the last (or the colour limits `clims`). Row 1 is at the top, as in the matrix. With `x` and `y`, the cells are placed at those coordinates.
syntax: With the cells' centres at `x` (across) and `y` (down).

examples.title: A correlation matrix with fixed limits

body: Draws an arrow with components `(u, v)` at each point `(x, y)`. The arrows are scaled so that the longest is about as long as the grid's spacing; a scale factor changes that, and `0` or `'off'` draws them at their own length.
syntax: Arrows `(u, v)` at the points `(x, y)`.
At the grid of row and column numbers.
Scaled by `scale` after the automatic scaling (0 for none).
With a line style and colour, and properties.

examples.title: A rotating field
The gradient of a function over its contours

body: Like `plot`, with a third coordinate. Drag in the figure to turn the view; `grid on` helps to read depth.
syntax: The points (x, y, z) joined in order.
With a line style, marker and colour.

examples.title: A helix
examples.code:
t = linspace(0, 6*pi, 300);
plot3(cos(t), sin(t), t/(2*pi))
grid on
xlabel('x')
ylabel('y')
zlabel('turns')

examples.title: Markers in space
examples.code:
rng default
P = randn(50, 3);
plot3(P(:, 1), P(:, 2), P(:, 3), 'o')
grid on
view(40, 25)
